mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the expected S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to tightened financing conditions that dampen corporate investment and consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns do not fall below the pre-trigger 20-day mean in any of the triggered months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a concurrent decline in new job openings (indirect proxy via INDPRO) signals a weakening labor market, which is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% while INDPRO decreases by >5% in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market weakening detected via dual indicator divergence
failure_condition: During the trigger period, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative in at least 70% of months (rolling 12-month average).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in both consumer confidence (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their prior month's levels predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it reflects strengthening economic momentum.
regime_hint: Recovery momentum in core US indicators
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, the 60-day forward returns do not outperform a 60-day rolling baseline by more than one standard deviation (IC > 0.67).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Industrial Production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months, despite stable or rising CPIAUCSL, indicates softening supply-side capacity, which is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for 3 consecutive months while CPIAUCSL does not rise by >2% in any of those months
failure_condition: During the 3-month contraction window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the UNRATE falls below 6.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a labor market softening that coincides with a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as markets anticipate easing monetary policy.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.5% in two consecutive months
regime_hint: Labor market slack detected via long-term unemployment rate
failure_condition: Over the next 60 days, the 5-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant positive excess return (IC < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous surge in employment (PAYEMS) and a decline in consumer sentiment (HOUST) suggests a labor market dislocation that precedes a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >8% while HOUST decreases by >12% in the same month
failure_condition: During the month of trigger, 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 80% of months in the subsequent 6-month window (rolling average).

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained period of falling inflation (CPIAUCSL) without a corresponding decline in FEDFUNDS, the S&P 500 60-day forward return tends to be positive as the market anticipates future rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by >0.5% for 3 consecutive months while FEDFUNDS remains flat or rises
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon following the trigger, 60-day forward returns do not exceed the prior 60-day average by more than one standard deviation (IC > 0.67).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in both industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales proxy (not available in the catalog; using RSAFS as a proxy for retail activity) below trend implies supply-demand imbalance, predicting negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >8% while RSAFS falls by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: During the triggered month, the 20-day forward return is not negative in at least 75% of months over the following 12 months (rolling average).
